proposals.evidence: Full upaviśati includes both the sitting verb and the upaviṣṭa past stem, including Apabhramsha baiṭṭha, Hindi baiṭhā/baiṭhnā, Old Marwari baithā and Gujarati bɛṭho. The selected standalone ṭ(h) forms fit that past-stem-based paradigm with ordinary imperative, participial or infinitive endings. The source’s aspiration and vowel notation is retained. The bas/bes forms, for which Turner also allows contamination or derivation from vasati, and merged son/sit records are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The complete response is baiṭh/beṭ “sit” plus jā “go” as an auxiliary, in source order. CDIAL 2245 explicitly includes the baiṭh/beṭ stem rebuilt on upaviṣṭa; 10452 gives the regional jā imperative and go verb. The segmentation is a compositional analysis of the survey response, not a claim that Turner lists the full modern construction. Ordinary imperative endings and the conjunctive i of the first member are accounted for. Responses containing another finite clause or unclear additional words are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The response contains the baiṭh/beṭ sitting stem plus the gayo/go go-perfect auxiliary. CDIAL 2245 accounts for the first member’s past-stem-based paradigm and 4008,1 for the second member, including regional contraction. Both ordered components are retained; this is a modern auxiliary construction, not a single inherited Sanskrit word. Mixed slash responses and additional unanalysed tense material are excluded.
